sentences.text: Yes, a dedicated discharge coordinator improved the discharge planning process and reduced problems experienced by patients after discharge in the study.

This conclusion rests on 600 randomly sampled adult medical patients discharged home from three medical wards, assessed before and after introducing a discharge coordinator over three study phases spanning 18 months.
The same study found no evidence that the coordinator improved the timeliness or effectiveness of community services after discharge or the appropriateness or efficiency of bed use.

The passages do not settle whether oral endotracheal intubation efficacy is impaired in the helicopter environment; they show longer in-flight intubation times and two esophageal intubations, but no significant difference in appropriate endotracheal intubation.

In flight nurses performing manikin intubations, the mean in-flight time was 25.9 +/- 10.9 seconds versus 13.2 +/- 2.8 seconds in the emergency department stretcher control setting (ANOVA, F = 38.7, p<.001).

All control intubations were placed correctly in the trachea, and there were two (6.7%) esophageal intubations in the in-flight setting, but the difference in appropriate endotracheal intubation was not significant (chi 2 = 0.3; p>0.05).
Yes, low serum chloride level was independently associated with higher cardiovascular mortality in a 10-year follow-up cohort.

In 4793 men and 4313 women aged 25-74 years free of symptomatic coronary heart disease at baseline, the adjusted risk ratio for cardiovascular disease death for those with serum chloride ≤100 mmol/l versus >100 mmol/l was 1.65 (95% CI 1.06–2.57) in men and 2.16 (95% CI 1.11–4.22) in women.
The adjusted risk ratios across four baseline serum chloride groups showed a decreasing log-linear dose-response relation to total and cardiovascular mortalities.
The review reports that perforation of the appendix is a risk factor for tubal infertility, but its ectopic pregnancy estimate is for appendectomy, not specifically perforation.

In a review of 4 studies with nonexposed control groups, the risk estimate was 4.8 (95% CI 1.5 to 14.9) for tubal infertility from perforation of the appendix and 1.6 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.5) for ectopic pregnancy after an appendectomy.
The review states that recall bias and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some reports weakened the validity of the studies.
No, variations in the use of carotid endarterectomy were not explained by population need as measured by district stroke mortality or stroke admission rates.

Across district populations in two English health regions, utilisation varied 14-fold, but standardised utilisation rates showed no association with district stroke mortality (r=-0.06, 95% CI -0.41 to 0.30) or admission rates for stroke (r=0.17, 95% CI -0.2 to 0.49).
Utilisation was strongly related to residence in districts where services were located and was lowest in the most affluent wards.
Yes, amoxapine meets the occupancy profile described for atypical antipsychotics.

In seven healthy volunteers given 50–250 mg/day amoxapine for 5 days, 5-HT2 receptors were near saturation at 100 mg/day and above, D2 receptor occupancies increased dose-dependently but never exceeded 80%, and 5-HT2 occupancy exceeded D2 occupancy at all doses.
These findings match the stated atypical antipsychotic criteria of high 5-HT2 occupancy and greater 5-HT2 than D2 occupancy.

The supplied passages do not settle whether the Barthel Index alone is an adequate measure of outcome The first study's objective was to consider whether the Barthel Index alone provides sufficient information about long term outcome, and its results compare Barthel Index scores with other outcome measures In that study, 123 (42%) people were known alive, 106 (86%) were interviewed, median age was 71 years (range 34-79), and mean interval between stroke and follow up was 4.9 years Barthel correlations were r=0.217 to r=0.810 across SF36 dimensions, r=-0.189 (sleep, NS) to r=-0.840 (physical mobility) across Nottingham health profile dimensions, r=-0.563 with the hospital anxiety and depression scale depression component, r=0.361 with the life satisfaction index, r=0.726 with the London handicap scale, and r=0.826 with the Frenchay activities index A separate study of 293 stroke survivors (ESD n=135, non-ESD n=158; 84 caregivers) used the Barthel Index as the primary outcome at baseline, 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months but did not compare Barthel alone with other outcome measures for adequacy
Yes, laparoscopic reoperation for failed antireflux surgery was feasible in the reported case series.

The results rest on 46 consecutive patients with previous antireflux procedures (21 laparoscopic, 21 laparotomy, 3 thoracotomy, and 1 thoracoscopy) who underwent laparoscopic reoperative procedures including Nissen fundoplication (n = 22), Toupet fundoplication (n = 13), paraesophageal hernia repair (n = 4), Dor procedure (n = 2), Angelchik prosthesis removal (n = 2), Heller myotomy (n = 2), and takedown of a wrap (n = 1).

The conversion rate from laparoscopic to open was 20% overall (9 patients) but 0% in the last 10 patients, and mortality was 0%, with a mean +/- SEM hospital stay of 2.3 +/- 0.9 days for operations completed laparoscopically.

Follow-up was possible in 35 patients (76%) at 17.2 +/- 11.8 months, the well-being score improved from 8.6 +/- 2.1 before to 2.9 +/- 2.4 after surgery (P<.001), and 31 (89%) of 35 patients were satisfied with their decision to have reoperation.

In 25 enrolled patients with angina on hypotensive medications and documented hypotension, 107 hypotensive events and 40 ST events occurred in 14 patients, and 14 hypotension-induced ischaemic events occurred in 8 patients.

Thirteen of the 14 hypotension-induced ischaemic events were preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure (median 57.5 mm Hg), and ST events were significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events (chi2=40.2, p<0.0001).
Patients with these events were more frequently taking multiple hypotensive drug regimens (8/8 v 9/17, chi2=5.54, p=0.022).

No, clinician assessment was not accurate enough to detect acute chest syndrome in febrile patients with sickle cell disease: overall physician sensitivity for predicting ACS was only 39%, and 61% (14/23) of ACS cases were not clinically suspected before chest radiography.

In 73 patients with sickle cell disease and 96 febrile events, 23 (24%) had chest radiograph evidence of ACS, and no symptom or physical examination finding helped identify ACS except splinting (4/23 [17%] versus 0/73 [0%]), while 57% of patients with ACS had completely normal physical examination findings.
Diagnostic accuracy did not improve significantly with increasing levels of pediatric training.
Yes, the NIHSS favors left hemisphere strokes in the sense that right-sided strokes have significantly lower acute NIHSS scores than left-sided strokes when adjusted for stroke volume.

In 153 patients with acute stroke who had MRI and NIHSS within 24 hours, for NIHSS scores of 0 to 5 the mean DWI lesion volume was 8.8 cm3 for right-sided strokes versus 3.2 cm3 for left-sided strokes (P=0.04), and among DWI lesions larger than 9 cm3, 8 of 37 right-sided strokes had NIHSS 0 to 5 versus 1 of 39 left-sided strokes (P=0.01).

In the placebo arm of the NINDS t-PA stroke trial, right hemisphere stroke volume was statistically greater than left hemisphere stroke volume after adjusting for baseline NIHSS (P<0.001), and for a 24-hour NIHSS of 16 to 20 the median volume was 133 mL for right versus 48 mL for left hemisphere strokes (P<0.001).
The supplied passages do not settle whether desflurane alters left ventricular function specifically during aortic surgery.

In 50 patients scheduled for vascular surgery, 16 developed hypertension at surgical incision, and desflurane controlled systolic arterial pressure in all 16 with a mean end-tidal concentration of 5.1+/-0.7%.

When desflurane was added to restore blood pressure, no change was noted in heart rate, cardiac index, mean pulmonary arterial pressure, stroke volume, end-diastolic and end-systolic cross-sectional areas, fractional area change, or left ventricular circumferential fiber shortening.

The passages do not directly show that the Mammography Quality Standards Act caused an effect on mammography quality in North Carolina; they show that the percentage of facilities meeting quality standards increased from the first inspection to the second inspection during MQSA implementation.

Among all North Carolina mammography facilities inspected in 1993-1994 and again in 1995, phantom image passing rate rose from 31.6% to 78.2%, darkroom fog passing rate rose from 74.3% to 88.5%, and developer temperature difference passing rate rose from 62.4% to 86.9%.
The MQSA of 1992 was implemented by the FDA, and the study examined its impact on mammography quality in North Carolina during 1995, its first year of implementation.

The supplied passages do not settle whether thrombosis prophylaxis in all hospitalised medical patients makes sense, because they report incidence and risk-stratification data rather than universal-prophylaxis outcomes.

In a general internal ward, symptomatic venous thrombosis occurred in 39/6332 patients (0.6%) overall, and the incidence was 2.7% (24/876) in patients with known malignancy versus 0.3% (15/5456) in those without malignancy, with a relative risk of 10.0 (95% CI 5.3–18.9).
The passages do not directly show whether abdominal CT is always necessary in intoxicated blunt trauma patients.

In 324 intoxicated blunt trauma patients with blood alcohol level >=80 mg/dL, Glasgow Coma Scale score 15, and unremarkable abdominal examination, 317 (98%) had CT scans negative for abdominal injury, 7 (2%) had abdominal injuries, and only 2 (0.6%) required abdominal exploration.
A significant association was found between major chest injury and abdominal injury.
Yes, head positioning influences anterior chamber depth in pseudoexfoliation syndrome.

In 39 patients with clinically apparent unilateral pseudoexfoliation and elevated intraocular pressure, anterior chamber depth in the pseudoexfoliative eyes decreased from a mean of 3.08 mm supine to 2.95 mm prone, while fellow eyes decreased from 3.01 mm to 2.97 mm.
The decrease in anterior chamber depth when facing down was significantly greater in the pseudoexfoliation eyes than in the fellow eyes.

The passages do not settle whether open access endoscopy closes the door to an adequately informed patient; they show that open access patients reported receiving significantly less information to help identify the procedure and less explanation concerning its nature than patients referred from a gastrointestinal subspecialty clinic.

In outpatients presenting for upper and lower endoscopy, open access patients reported less identifying information (p<0.01) and less explanation of the procedure's nature (p<0.005) than the GI subspecialty clinic group.
The other supplied passages on open-access endoscopy address guideline appropriateness and referral indications, not patient information.
No—visual loss in amblyopia was not permanent in the reported cases, because amblyopic eyes showed improvement in acuity that remained stable over follow-up.
Among 12 detected cases, 9 had a history of amblyopia in the eye that improved.
The mean improvement in amblyopic eyes by 12 months was 3.3 lines for distance acuity and 1.9 lines for near acuity in logMAR.
Improvement generally occurred between 1 and 12 months from baseline and remained stable over the follow-up period.
No, patients with Werlhof's disease were not observed to have increased bleeding complications when undergoing cardiac surgery in the supplied case-control study.

In 10 WD patients (eight males, two females) each matched to five no-WD patients, total drainage loss via mediastinal chest tubes was almost identical (1140 ml in the WD group vs 1197 ml in the no-WD group).
One patient in each group had a bleeding complication requiring reexploration.
WD patients had significantly lower platelet counts and received significantly more platelet concentrates (mean 2.3 vs 0.7, P=0.007).

The passages do not settle whether long-term continuation is needed, but they show that over 1 year stopping folic acid in rheumatoid arthritis patients established on methotrexate <20 mg weekly and folic acid 5 mg daily increased early study discontinuation (46% placebo vs 21% continued folic acid, P=0.02) and nausea at 9 months (45% vs 7%, P=0.001).
Two patients in the placebo group discontinued because of neutropenia.
The placebo group had significantly lower disease activity on a few variables, but these were probably not of clinical significance.
The supplied passages do not settle whether antiphospholipid antibodies play a role in avascular necrosis of bone in SLE.

In a cohort of 265 SLE patients followed from 1978 to 1998, 11 had AVN, giving a point prevalence of 4%, and there were no significant differences in the presence of individual antiphospholipid antibodies (IgM and IgG anticardiolipin antibodies and lupus anticoagulant) or their combination between the AVN group and the two control groups.
The objective was to investigate aPL status with adjustment for corticosteroid use as risk factors for AVN, but the reported result is only the absence of significant differences.
Other supplied passages address aPL specificity for aPL-related events and aPL associations with thrombosis, fetal loss, and thrombocytopenia in SLE/APS, not AVN.
The supplied passages do not settle whether APACHE II is a reliable marker of physiological impairment in emergency surgical patients.
In 85 consecutive emergency surgical patients, the mean APACHE II score at ICU admission was 24.2 +/- 8.3, approximately 36% greater than the initial pre-surgery score of 17.8 +/- 7.7 (P<.001).

The predicted mortality of 50% from the ICU-admission APACHE II score was significantly different from the observed mortality rate of 32% (P=.02), while the predicted mortality of 34% from the initial APACHE II score favorably corresponded with the observed 32%.
In 40 long-term patients (>/=10 days in the ICU), the difference between APACHE II scores of survivors and patients who died was statistically significant on day 10 (P=.04).
The passages do not settle whether antral follicle assessment is a better predictor of IVF outcome than age and FSH.
19%), and this difference remained significant after controlling for patient age and basal FSH.
1%), while cancellation was also significantly increased with advancing maternal age and elevated basal FSH.
The supplied passages do not settle whether patient position during liver surgery influences the risk of venous air embolism.

In 10 patients during liver surgery, horizontal, 20-degree head-up, and 20-degree head-down positions showed no demonstrable pressure gradient between hepatic and central venous levels, with absolute pressures highest head-down and lowest head-up and no negative intraluminal pressure recorded.
The background states only a general belief that head-down tilt decreases the likelihood of venous air embolism during liver resection, while no embolism outcome is reported.

Other supplied passages concern intrahepatic air during porcine liver procurement , portal vein embolization , and liver damage from penetrating abdominal firearm injury , not patient position and venous air embolism risk.
Managed care had only marginal effects on the likelihood of having a usual source of care for privately insured and Medicaid beneficiaries.
Yes, the manic/mixed episode distinction runs true over time in bipolar disorder patients.

This finding rests on patients with three or more entries in a community mental health center management information system (N=241) and their manic and mixed episodes (N=1,224) over an 11-year period.

The observed distribution of manic and mixed episodes was compared to the expected distribution from averaging 1,000 randomly generated simulations, and episodes were consistent (all manic or all mixed) in significantly more patients than would be expected by chance.

Yes, in children with malignancy and ARDS, some respiratory variables distinguished outcome: peak inspiratory pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure, and ventilation index values could distinguish outcome by day 3, and PaO2/FIO2 and P(A-a)O2 showed a significant relationship with outcome from day 8 after onset of mechanical ventilation.
The study included 17 children with ARDS and malignancy, aged 10.5 +/- 5.1 years, who needed mechanical ventilation.
Six of the 17 children (35.3%) survived, and sepsis syndrome was present in 70.6%.
The comparison was between outcomes based on those respiratory measurements.

Yes, a serious acute side effect occurred in 1 of 65 patients (2%, 95% CI 0%-8%) who received polyvalent antivenin for rattlesnake bites at doses up to 30 vials (mean 12.0 ± 6.0; 66% received ≥10 vials) and required intravenous epinephrine for blood pressure support.
Acute side effects within 6 hours occurred in 12 patients (18%, 95% CI 10%-30%) and consisted solely of urticaria in all but that 1 patient.
The 65 patients were identified from a total of 73 patients with rattlesnake bites.
No deaths, amputations, or permanent disability occurred in the patients receiving antivenin.
No, increasing nerve length within the treatment volume did not improve pain relief in trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery.

In 87 patients with typical trigeminal neuralgia randomized to one (n = 44) or two (n = 43) isocenters, the actuarial rate of complete pain relief was 67.7% ± 5.1% and was identical for one- and two-isocenter radiosurgery.

Complications (numbness or paresthesias) correlated with the nerve length irradiated (p = 0.018), while improved pain relief correlated with younger age (p = 0.025) and fewer prior procedures (p = 0.039).

In 130 children suspected of having inflammatory bowel disease, the final diagnosis was Crohn's disease in 27, ulcerative colitis in nine, miscellaneous colitis in 13, probably normal in 42, and normal in 39.
A separate study included 49 patients with Crohn's disease, 16 spouses, and 151 first-degree relatives who underwent fecal calprotectin testing.
The supplied passages do not settle whether alexithymia is a risk factor for unexplained physical symptoms in general medical outpatients.

In a cross-sectional study of 321 patients attending an internal medicine outpatient clinic, 169 had medically unexplained physical symptoms after complete physical examinations, and overall these patients were not more alexithymic.
However, patients with both unexplained symptoms and a mental disorder who denied any possible connection between emotional problems and their physical symptoms did have more alexithymic traits.

Another passage states alexithymia has been associated with increased reporting of medically unexplained symptoms, but its samples were students and intensive outpatients/residents in an anxiety disorder treatment program, not general medical outpatients.

The supplied passages show an association between delay in transfer to rehabilitation and longer total hospital length of stay, but do not directly show that delay affects outcome after proximal femur fracture.
In 455 patients aged over 75 with proximal femur fracture, 58% were transferred to a rehabilitation ward.
For those transferred, only age predicted discharge to a more dependent residence, with a relative risk of 1.47 (95% CI 1.15-1.88) for people aged over 85 compared with younger people.
Delay in transfer was associated with a longer total hospital length of stay of 0.64 (95% CI 0.23-1.05) days per day of delay.
The other supplied passage concerns proximal humerus fractures, not proximal femur.

No, clinical variables did not accurately predict pathologic radiographs in children with a first episode of wheezing, because a discriminant analysis correctly predicted only 15% of pathologic radiographs.

In a prospective convenience sample of children with a first episode of wheezing, 61 patients (9%) had pathologic radiographs, and between the pathologic and nonpathologic groups the only significant difference was pretreatment oxygen saturation.

Clinical score, respiratory rate, and presence of rales both pretreatment and posttreatment were not significantly different between groups, and the model correctly predicted 90% of nonpathologic radiographs but only 15% of pathologic radiographs.
The supplied passages do not settle whether hepatitis G virus or TT virus are involved in cryptogenic chronic liver disease.

In 23 patients with cryptogenic chronic liver disease versus 40 with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease, HGV-RNA was detected in 4/23 versus 6/40 (17.4% vs 15%, p=ns), and at least one HGV marker in 6/23 versus 16/40 (26.1% vs 40%, p=ns).
TTV-DNA was present in serum in only 3 subjects overall, 1 with cryptogenic and 2 with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease.

Demographic and clinical features, including stage and grade of liver histology, were comparable between HGV-infected and uninfected subjects, while severe liver damage was significantly more frequent in subjects with hepatitis C virus liver disease.

The supplied results do not directly show that hospice care improves pain management; they show that hospice recipients were more likely to receive regular treatment for daily pain than nonhospice residents.
The comparison was among dying nursing home residents with daily pain near the end of life, comprising 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents.

Fifteen percent of hospice residents versus 23% of nonhospice residents received no analgesics (OR=0.57, 95% CI=0.45-0.74), and 21% versus 29% received analgesics not recommended by AMDA (OR=0.65, 95% CI=0.52-0.80).

Fifty-one percent of hospice residents versus 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain, and controlling for clinical confounders hospice residents were twice as likely to receive regular treatment (adjusted OR=2.08, 95% CI=1.68-2.56).
The supplied passages do not settle whether escalation of the apical dose changes treatment outcome in beta-radiation of posterior choroidal melanomas with 106Ru plaques.
Its methods report 48 patients treated with ruthenium plaques, with a median apical dose of 120 Gy and a median scleral dose of 546 Gy.
Its results report 90% local control, 90% overall 5-year survival, 6% second ruthenium application, and 10% enucleation after 5.8 years of follow-up, without comparing outcomes by apical dose level.
The supplied passages do not settle whether rugby headgear prevents concussion.
In a questionnaire of 63 players from four Canadian teams, 62% of players and 33% of coaches believed headgear could prevent concussion, while only 27% of players reported wearing it.
A pediatric emergency department study followed children aged 8 to 17 years discharged with concussion but did not assess rugby headgear.
In bicyclists, no association was found for concussion only with facial fractures.
The passages do not settle whether pulmonary valve replacement in adults late after repair of tetralogy of Fallot is too late.
They show that chronic pulmonary regurgitation after repair of tetralogy of Fallot leads to RV dilation and an increased incidence of sudden cardiac death in adult patients.

They also show 14 patients who underwent pulmonary valve replacement with a mechanical valved conduit, all with a mean of 3.0 +/- 1.2 previous operations, including 7 patients previously operated on for tetralogy of Fallot, with short-term results evaluated.
No supplied passage directly compares early versus late pulmonary valve replacement or reports outcomes by timing in this population.

The passages do not settle whether the inter-arm blood pressure difference can predict the severity of subclavian steal syndrome; they show that systolic blood pressure difference was significantly higher in the complete reversal and alternating flow groups than in the systolic deceleration group (P<.001).

This came from 51 ultrasonography studies in 49 patients with sonographically proven SSS (17 men, 32 women; mean age 65.3 +/- 10.5 years), with waveform analysis showing complete reversal in 16 (31%), alternating flow in 24 (47%), and systolic deceleration in 11 (22%).
The comparison was the side-to-side systolic blood pressure difference (normal-side minus lesion-side) across those three vertebral artery waveform types.

The passages do not settle whether a retinal haemorrhage after convulsions should prompt further investigation; they show that among 153 children aged 2 months to 2 years seen after a convulsive episode, 1 child had unilateral retinal haemorrhages following a simple febrile convulsion, and a thorough investigation uncovered no other reason for the finding.
The study was prompted because the prevalence of retinal haemorrhages after convulsions is not well established and these haemorrhages are considered characteristic of child abuse.

In 601 patients aged >=65 years with cardiogenic shock, 287 were admitted to hospitals without revascularization services and 314 to hospitals with coronary angioplasty and coronary artery bypass surgery facilities.
After adjustment, the odds ratios were 0.83 (95% CI 0.47, 1.45) for 30-day mortality and 0.91 (95% CI 0.49, 1.72) for 1-year mortality.
No, postoperative antibiotics had no role in pain control, postoperative fever, secondary hemorrhage, or reduction in hospital stay in a tonsillectomy audit.
That audit included 185 patients who underwent tonsillectomy with or without adenoidectomy, ages 2 to 53 years, with the majority being children.
No, the results indicate there is no need for pelvic CT scan in the pre-operative evaluation of renal cell carcinoma because all pelvic abnormalities were detected by other investigations before CT.
In 400 patients with RCC, 14 (3.5%) had an abnormality on pelvic CT: 5 (1.25%) category 1, 3 (0.75%) category 2, and 6 (1.5%) category 3.
However, all these pelvic abnormalities were detected prior to CT by ultrasound or plain x-ray.
Of the six malignant cases, two had superficial bladder cancer, one had RCC in a pelvic kidney, and three had bone metastases in the pelvis.

The supplied passages do not settle whether a special interest in laparoscopy affects the treatment of acute cholecystitis, but they show that care by laparoscopic specialists was associated with a higher rate of successful laparoscopic treatment.

Among 170 patients undergoing cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis, 48 were cared for by three laparoscopic specialists and 122 by nine general surgeons who perform only laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

Successful laparoscopic treatment occurred in 31 of 48 laparoscopic-specialist patients (65%) versus 44 of 122 general-surgeon patients (36%; p=0.001), and laparoscopic-specialist group status was a significant predictor of successful laparoscopic operation on logistic regression (p<0.01).

Median postoperative hospital stay was shorter in the laparoscopic-specialist group (3 vs 5 days; p<0.01), but laparoscopic-specialist status was not a significant predictor of prolonged length of stay after adjustment (p=0.21), and postoperative complication proportions were similar (31% vs 37%; p=0.6).
Yes, mossy fibers release GABA.

In hippocampal slices from 3- to 5-week-old guinea pigs, electrical stimuli that recruited dentate granule cells elicited monosynaptic GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic signals in CA3 pyramidal neurons, and these inhibitory signals satisfied the criteria that distinguish mossy fiber-CA3 synapses.
Mossy fiber terminals also show intense immunoreactivity for GABA and GAD67.
The supplied passages do not settle whether lipids, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking confer equal risk of myocardial infarction in women and men.

One study reports that systolic blood pressure was a stronger risk factor for women, fasting blood glucose ≥6.7 mmol/L identified higher risk for women (HR 2.65) than men (HR 2.08), self-reported diabetes did as well, triglyceride risk was significantly higher for women, and smoking increased risk two- to five-fold for women versus a doubling in men, while serum cholesterol was a significant risk factor for both sexes with hazard ratios decreasing with age.

A meta-analysis of CHD death found relative risks for systolic blood pressure, serum total cholesterol, smoking, and diabetes varied significantly across studies (p<0.05 for homogeneity) but did not compare women with men.

The MI-specific passage reports that patients with myocardial infarction were older and mostly women, with hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and smoking frequencies, but it does not compare risk by sex.
Diabetes Prospective Study.

Among 5,088 of 5,102 participants grouped by fasting plasma glucose at diagnosis (<140, 140 to <180, or >=180 mg/dl), those in the lowest category had fewer cases of retinopathy, abnormal biothesiometer measurements, and reported erectile dysfunction.

The low fasting plasma glucose group had a significantly reduced risk for each predefined clinical outcome except stroke, and the intermediate group had significantly reduced risk for each outcome except stroke and myocardial infarction.
Both low and intermediate fasting plasma glucose groups had significantly reduced risk for progression of retinopathy, reduction in vibration sensory threshold, or development of microalbuminuria.
The rate of increase in fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c during the study was identical in all three groups, although absolute differences persisted.
The supplied passages do not settle whether increased neutrophil migratory activity after major trauma is a factor in the etiology of ARDS.

In 17 adult blunt trauma patients with Injury Severity Score >=18, neutrophils isolated at admission and 8 and 24 hrs later migrated in significantly greater numbers to interleukin-8 at 30 and 100 ng/mL than neutrophils from 9 normal laboratory volunteers (Mann-Whitney U test, p<.05).
Neutrophil counts in whole blood from patients who later developed ARDS were significantly elevated at admission and declined rapidly over the next 24 hrs.
The supplied passages do not settle whether withdrawal-induced anxiety in alcoholism is based on beta-endorphin deficiency.

They show that beta-endorphin was significantly lowered on day 1 and day 14 of alcohol withdrawal relative to controls in 60 alcoholics versus 30 healthy volunteers, and that beta-endorphin levels were inversely correlated with self-rated anxiety on day 1 (r=-0.58) and day 14 (r=-0.71).
Partial correlation coefficients controlling for ACTH plasma levels revealed that this correlation was largely independent from ACTH.

The passages do not settle whether muscle power is related to running speed with changes of direction: in the relevant study, correlations between concentric leg muscle power and speed while changing direction were generally low and non-significant, while some moderate and significant (p<0.05) coefficients were found for reactive strength.

This was in 15 male participants free of injury with recent experience competing in sports involving sprints with changes of direction, who were timed in 8 m sprints in a straight line and with various changes of direction and tested for leg extensor concentric power by an isokinetic squat and reactive strength by a drop jump.
The supplied passages do not settle whether HELLP syndrome is evidence of a possible systemic inflammatory response in pre-eclampsia, because they report no inflammatory measures.
They compare neonatal outcome among 269 pregnancies with HELLP syndrome, partial HELLP syndrome, or severe preeclampsia.
Another passage compared 62 preeclamptic women with first-cousin unions to 624 controls for outcomes including HELLP syndrome.
A further passage described 134 HELLP pregnancies by time of day and biochemical parameters.
Therefore these passages do not answer the question.

Yes, in patients in whom respiratory jugular venodilation is not identified, prepuncture ultrasound facilitates internal jugular vein cannulation, but no difference was shown in those in whom it is identified.

In 240 adults undergoing general anesthesia randomized to landmark or prepuncture ultrasound for right internal jugular vein cannulation, 188 had respiratory jugular venodilation identified and showed no significant differences in first-attempt cannulation (83.5% vs 85.7%), success within 3 attempts (96.9% vs 95.6%), or arterial puncture (1.0% vs 3.3%).

In the 52 patients without identified respiratory jugular venodilation, ultrasound produced significantly better access (86.2% vs 30.4%, p<0.001) and success (100% vs 78.3%, p<0.05) and no arterial punctures versus 13.0% in the landmark group.

In 260 women with measurable metastatic breast cancer fulfilling high-risk criteria and previously untreated for metastatic disease, mitoxantrone 12 mg/m(2) was compared with fluorouracil 500 mg/m(2), epirubicin 50 mg/m(2) and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m(2) (FEC) every 3 weeks.

The final evaluation showed no significant difference in response, objective remission rate, remission duration, time to response, time to best response, time to progression or overall survival, but a significant difference in gain from treatment using a modified Brunner's score favored the single-agent treatment arm.
Yes, ibuprofen increased perioperative blood loss in patients undergoing total hip replacement pretreated for 2 weeks before surgery.
In a double-blind, randomized comparison of 50 patients scheduled for total hip replacement, perioperative blood loss increased by 45% in the ibuprofen group compared with placebo.
Total blood loss was 1161 (±472) mL in the ibuprofen group versus 796 (±337) mL in the placebo group.
Yes, a written information sheet improved recall by patients.

In a prospective randomised controlled study of 126 patients undergoing revision or primary total hip arthroplasty, patients given written information plus appropriate explanation scored significantly higher on recall (48% correct answers) than patients given verbal information alone (38% correct answers).
The comparison included 65 patients given verbal information and 61 patients given written information, with recall tested by questionnaire on admission a mean of 18 days later.

In 11,661 veterans discharged with a primary diagnosis of congestive heart failure, the adjusted 1-year risk of death relative to mixed general medicine and cardiology care was 1.12 (0.94-1.34) for cardiology-only, 1.26 (1.15-1.38) for general medicine-only, and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) for neither.
The overall 1-year mortality rate was 23%, and a second cohort showed consistent survival differences between general medicine-only and mixed care (1.25 [1.14-1.37]).

The passages do not settle whether BMI influences morbidity and long-term survival in gastric cancer patients after gastrectomy, because only stage-specific survival results are reported and no morbidity results are given.

In gastric cancer patients who had undergone gastrectomy with D2-lymphadenectomy, those with BMI <0.185 had significantly longer mean survival than those with BMI >0.210 in stage 2 (1667 vs 1322 days, P=0.0240), while the higher BMI group had significantly longer mean survival in stage 3a (1431 vs 943 days, P=0.0071).
Morbidity was stated as compared between the two BMI groups, but no morbidity results are provided.
The supplied passages do not settle whether circumcision should be performed in childhood.

In 350 infants, complications including meatal deformities, meatal stenosis, adhesions and infection were more frequent and more significant in 250 neonates circumcised at 1 to 4 days than in 100 infants circumcised at 5 months.

Of 128 parents/children responding, 108 (84%) were satisfied with function and 102 (80%) reported a good cosmetic outcome; triple incision as preputioplasty would be recommended to other parents by 119 (93%), and 91 (71%) feared disadvantages in their son's later life if the child had been circumcised.

One study's stated aim was to evaluate prepuce development and retractibility and to point out the value of circumcision and prepucial forced dilation during childhood, but no outcome results are supplied.
Yes, in one reported case, spinal subdural hematoma (SSDH) followed subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) from a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm.

The patient was a 52-year-old woman who underwent craniotomy for the ruptured aneurysm and on the sixth postoperative day developed severe lower back and buttock pain, with MRI showing a lumbosacral subdural hematoma.
She had no neurologic symptoms other than sciatica, was treated conservatively, and the hematoma diminished completely 15 weeks later; she was discharged 7 weeks later without neurologic deficit.
Yes, several environmental factors were significantly associated with primary systemic vasculitis (PSV) in the supplied results.

In 75 PSV cases compared with 273 controls, farming in the index year was associated with PSV (odds ratio 2.3, 95% CI 1.2-4.6), as were farming during working lifetime (2.2, 1.2-3.8), high occupational silica exposure in the index year (3.0, 1.0-8.4), high occupational solvent exposure during working lifetime (2.7, 1.1-6.6), drug allergy (3.6, 1.8-7.0), and allergy overall (2.2, 1.2-3.9).
No other significant associations were found.
The supplied results do not directly establish that anorectal endosonography is clinically valuable in dyschesia, but they show it can demonstrate dysfunction.

In 20 patients with dyschesia versus 20 healthy controls, the anal sphincter became paradoxically shorter and/or thicker during straining in 85% vs 35% (p<0.01), and the m. puborectalis did so in 80% vs 30% (p<0.01).
Changes in sphincter length and in m. puborectalis length and thickness were significantly different between groups (p<0.01).

Yes, in selected patients, a decision-analysis model found that anticoagulation could be preferred for prior deep hemispheric ICH when the risk of thromboembolic stroke is particularly high, but withholding anticoagulation was strongly preferred for prior lobar ICH and was also preferred for prior deep hemispheric ICH in the base case.

That model compared warfarin with no anticoagulation in a base-case 69-year-old man with a history of ICH and newly diagnosed nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, and withholding anticoagulation improved quality-adjusted life expectancy by 1.9 QALYs for prior lobar ICH and 0.3 QALYs for prior deep hemispheric ICH.
No, tumor depth should not be included as an independent prognostic factor when grade and size are taken into account.

In a population-based series of 490 adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma of the extremity or trunk wall and at least 4.5 years of follow-up, multivariate analysis showed no major prognostic effect of tumor depth after accounting for grade and size.

Tumor depth influenced prognosis only in the subset of high-grade and large tumors, where deep-seated tumors had poorer survival, but this was explained by the larger mean size of deep-seated tumors, which were one third larger than large superficial tumors.
Yes, a 9-month treatment was sufficient in the patients with tuberculous enterocolitis studied.
In 40 patients randomized prospectively, 22 received 9 months and 18 received 15 months of anti-tuberculous therapy.
Complete response was obtained in all patients in both groups, and no recurrence of active intestinal tuberculosis occurred during follow-up in either group.
Two patients in the 9-month group and one in the 15-month group underwent operation due to intestinal obstruction and perianal fistula, respectively.
In lung cancer patients, lower socioeconomic status was associated with worse quality of life at baseline but not at three months after initial treatment.

Of 129 newly diagnosed patients, 82 had complete baseline and follow-up data, and 57% were of lower socioeconomic status and had more health problems, less functioning, and more symptoms than affluent patients.
At baseline, significant differences were found for physical mobility (P = 0.05), energy (P = 0.01), role functioning (P = 0.04), physical functioning (P = 0.03), and breathlessness (P = 0.02).
At follow-up, there was no significant difference between patient groups and no consistent pattern emerged.
Yes, in CD Fischer rats, Nd:YAG laser-induced thermo therapy (LITT) of the left forebrain opened the blood-brain barrier locoregionally, and HPLC proved paclitaxel passage across the disrupted BBB.
The passages do not settle whether this is an effective adjuvant glioma therapy; they show locoregional extravasation of Evans blue, C3C, fibrinogen, and IgM after LITT.

The bottom line rests on CD Fischer rats subjected to LITT of the left forebrain, with BBB disruption assessed by Evans blue and immunohistochemistry and paclitaxel content compared between brain and plasma samples by HPLC, but no numerical effect sizes are reported.

The supplied passages do not settle whether cell death in mesial temporal sclerosis is apoptotic; in temporal lobe specimens from 15 drug-resistant epilepsy patients with MTS (six women, nine men; mean age 29 +/- 8 years), increased Bax immunopositivity and fractin in approximately 10% of neurons indicated some caspase activity, but TUNEL showed no DNA fragmentation and no typical apoptotic nuclear changes were detected.
That study compared MTS tissue with normal adult brain, where Bcl-2 immunoreactivity was absent but was seen in some remaining MTS neurons and most reactive astroglia.
In that study, early discharge was defined as discharge between 24 and 47 hours of age, and 1324 early discharge and 2536 traditional stay infants were compared.

Early discharge infants had a higher rate of initial filter paper specimens being inadequate (22.9%) than traditional stay infants (14.3%, P<.0001), but a higher rate of repeat specimens when the initial specimen was inadequate (85.0% vs 75.3%, P=.002) and a higher rate of an adequate specimen within the first 9 days (98.8% vs 96.7%, P=.0005).
A separate South Australian analysis reported that missed screening was associated with early discharge from hospital before 3 days, especially less than 1 day.

The passages do not settle whether progression of valvar aortic stenosis can be predicted accurately, but they show that progression rate depends on valvar calcification and initial aortic valve area.

In 169 men and 88 women with aortic stenosis, progression rate was dependent on valvar calcification score 0 to III and exponentially correlated with aortic valve opening area at initial catheterization, while age, sex, and etiology did not significantly influence progression.

The reported thresholds were AVA below 0.75 cm2 with VC=0, 0.8 with VC=I, 0.9 with VC=II, or 1.0 with VC=III, at which it is probable that aortic stenosis will require operation in the following years.
Yes, a 2-day course on communication with terminally ill patients was followed by participants' self-reported increases in sense of security and changes in communication behavior.

The first three courses were attended by 31 participants, who assessed their own sense of security in seven communication settings on a visual analog scale at the beginning and end of the course and 3 months afterwards, with important increases for communicating a diagnosis of cancer with good or less good prognosis, recurrence of cancer, or far progressive cancer without curative approach.
Three months after the course, participants described multiple changes indicating increased sensibility and professionalism in communication behavior.
No, based on these results, histological sub-classification had no demonstrated prognostic value in children with cerebellar astrocytoma.

In children aged 0-14 years treated in Denmark from 1960-1984 and followed to January 2001 or death, overall survival was 81% after 15-40 years, and no difference in survival time was demonstrated between pilocytic astrocytoma and fibrillary astrocytoma, while the Kernohan and WHO classification systems had no predictive value and the Daumas-Duport system was unsuitable as a prognostic tool for low-grade posterior fossa astrocytomas.
The significant positive prognostic factors instead were surgically gross-total removal and location of the tumour in the cerebellum proper as opposed to location in the fourth ventricle.
The passages do not settle whether a practicing surgeon can reliably detect early lymphedema.
They report circumference-based detection in 90 breast cancer patients followed quarterly for 3 years, with 39 lymphedema cases identified by the academic trial.
Sensitivity was 37% for a 10% circumference increase at two sites, 49% for a 10% increase at any site, and 91% for a 5% increase at any site.
A separate passage describes a risk nomogram for lymphedema after axillary lymph node dissection.
Another describes HR MRL in three patients with lower-extremity lymphedema.

Yes, breast cancer survival has improved over time in the populations reported, with a statistically significant unadjusted improvement among women with recurrent breast cancer and a reported considerable improvement among patients diagnosed before age 50.

In 834 women who developed recurrent breast cancer between November 1974 and December 2000 and were divided into five consecutive groups by year of recurrence, more recent cohorts had longer survival in the unadjusted analysis (P<0.001), and the multivariate analysis showed a trend toward improved survival with a 1% reduction in risk for each increasing year.

For patients diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 years, prognosis improved considerably during past decades, with latest period-analysis estimates of cumulative 40-year relative survival of approximately 43% for all cancers combined, 57% for localized cancers, and 24% for regional tumor spread.
Yes, patients with prostate cancer who developed ≤5 metastatic lesions had superior survival compared with those who developed >5 lesions.
The analysis included 369 patients with Stage T1-T3aN0-NXM0 prostate cancer treated with curative external beam radiotherapy, of whom 74 (20%) developed metastases.
Patients with ≤5 metastatic lesions had 5- and 10-year overall survival rates of 73% and 36%, versus 45% and 18% for patients with >5 lesions (p=0.02).
Metastasis-free survival and the interval from diagnosis to bone metastasis were also statistically superior for patients with ≤5 lesions compared with >5 lesions (p=0.01 and 0.02, respectively).
Survival after bone metastasis and the interval from bone metastasis diagnosis to death were not significantly different between the groups (p=0.17 and 0.27, respectively).

Yes, pain is a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry, with a point prevalence of about 50%, a 6-month prevalence of 75.5%, and a 12-month prevalence of 76.5% among 106 patients primarily diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder in general adult psychiatry.
Almost 10% of all patients reported pain continuing at least 3 months in the past year, and impairment and unfitness for work were related to specific psychiatric diagnosis.
The most frequent complaints were low back pain, headache, and shoulder and neck pain.
The supplied passages do not settle whether the sequence of clamp application during open abdominal aortic aneurysm surgery influences distal embolisation.

In 40 patients randomised to first clamping of the proximal aorta or the iliac vessels, the number of emboli detected through the superficial femoral arteries with a transcranial Doppler system showed no significant difference between groups (p=0.49).
The passages do not directly show that CT predicts the level of CSF block, but they show that a CT finding—third ventricle shape—correlates with the type of hydrocephalus.
In 50 children with communicating and 34 children with non-communicating hydrocephalus classified by air-encephalography, the only CT finding that correlated with type was third ventricle shape.
Significantly more children with non-communicating hydrocephalus had a rounded third ventricle than those with communicating hydrocephalus.
The supplied passages do not directly establish whether double reading of barium enemas is necessary.
In 994 consecutive barium enemas, adding a second reader increased the number of positive results from 249 to 315 (p<0.0001) and potentially altered clinical treatment in 98 patients (9.9%).

Sensitivity of the first and combined readings for detection of all lesions was identical at 76.3% (95% CI, 65.4-87.1%), while specificity decreased from 91.0% (95% CI, 87.9-94.3%) to 86.4% (95% CI, 82.2-90.0%) and agreement decreased from a kappa value of 61.8 to 52.9.
The second reading required an average of 3.3 min.
Yes, fear of anaphylaxis and/or dissemination was the main reason given by surgeons for not using percutaneous or laparoscopic treatment of liver hydatid cyst.

In a survey of 30 surgeons in northern Jordan, only 3 (10%) considered laparoscopy as the first line of treatment, and of the 27 who did not consider percutaneous or laparoscopic treatment, 21 (78%) gave fear of anaphylaxis and/or dissemination as the main reason for not using minimal-access techniques.
Yes, among women treated with radiotherapy for Hodgkin's disease, treatment around the time of pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.

In 382 women, 14 developed breast cancer, and the pregnant group had an overall incidence of 16.0% versus 2.3% in nonpregnant women (p=0.0001), with 10- and 15-year actuarial rates of 6.7% and 32.6% versus 0.4% and 1.7%, respectively.

In multivariate analysis, pregnancy around the time of radiotherapy was the only variable associated with increased risk, and women irradiated during pregnancy or within 1 month of pregnancy had a hazard ratio of 22.49 (95% CI, 5.56-90.88; p<0.001) compared with nonpregnant women and women irradiated later than 1 month after pregnancy.

No, patients with diabetes are not receiving exactly the same message from dietitians and nurses, based on a comparison of registered dietitian (RD) and registered nurse (RN) certified diabetes educators.

In a survey of 366 CDEs (207 RNs and 159 RDs), no statistically significant differences were found between RNs and RDs in typical carbohydrate recommendations for diabetes, but RDs were more likely than RNs to make recommendations for fiber intake or use of the glycemic index, and RNs were more likely than RDs to recommend consuming a carbohydrate source with protein to treat hypoglycemia.
The passages do not settle whether higher rates of depression in women are accounted for by differential symptom reporting.

In a population-based 13-year follow-up of 1727 community-dwelling adults, there were no significant gender differences in self-report of depression symptoms after adjusting for age, ethnicity, education, marital status, and employment, with an example that women were no more likely to endorse sadness than men (adjusted direct effect = 0.105, 95% CI -0.113 to 0.323).
No, acute changes in heart rate produced by isoproterenol did not affect aortic stiffness in patients with hypertension.

In 17 hypertensive patients (mean age 59 +/- 9 years), pulse wave velocity, compliance, and compliance index were grouped by every 10% increase in deltaHR, and there was no significant difference among groups in deltaPWV, deltaC, or deltaCi (p>0.05 for each).

Regression analysis showed no significant correlation of deltaHR with deltaPWV or deltaC (r = 0.18 and 0.13, p>0.05 for each). deltaCi had a poor correlation with deltaHR (r = 0.22, p<0.05), but only 4.6% of deltaCi could be referred to deltaHR (r2 = 0.046).
Yes, the supplied results support the Omega-3 Index (RBC EPA + DHA) as a new risk factor for death from coronary heart disease, showing it was inversely associated with CHD mortality.
An Omega-3 Index of >=8% was associated with the greatest cardioprotection, whereas an index of <=4% was associated with the least.
The comparison was therefore >=8% versus <=4%, evaluated in clinical/laboratory experiments and published primary and secondary prevention studies, especially for sudden cardiac death.
Yes, c-Kit-dependent growth of uveal melanoma cells is a potential therapeutic target based on the cell-line results.

In the three uveal melanoma cell lines OCM-1, OCM-3, and 92-1, c-Kit was strongly expressed and tyrosine phosphorylated, and all three expressed the c-kit ligand, suggesting autocrine/paracrine stimulation.
Treatment with STI571, which blocks c-kit autophosphorylation, resulted in cell death, and the IC50 for inhibition of c-kit phosphorylation and cell proliferation were equal and less than 2.5 µM.
Among 134 paraffin-embedded uveal melanomas, 84 expressed c-kit, and 6 of 8 fresh-frozen samples expressed c-kit.

Yes, the type of remission after a major depressive episode was an important risk factor for relapse over more than 4 years. In a sample of 139 Spanish outpatients with a unipolar major depressive episode, the relapse rate was 91.4% in the partial remission group compared with 51.3% in the complete remission group. The four factors with predictive relapse value were partial remission versus complete remission, intensity of clinical symptoms, age, and number of previous depressive episodes, and partial remission was the most powerful predictive factor.

In pooled individual data from stroke patients in two randomised controlled trials of intramuscular botulinum toxin, maximum change in a Composite Spasticity Index and maximum change in a Composite Functional Index occurred concurrently in 47 patients, spasticity improvement preceded function improvement in 26, and function improvement preceded spasticity improvement in 18.
Across 137 patients there was a definite relationship between maximum change in spasticity and maximum change in arm function, independent of treatment (rho = -0.2822, p = 0.0008).

Clear relationships were seen in patients treated with botulinum toxin (Dysport) at 500 or 1000 units (rho = -0.5679, p = 0.0090, n = 22; rho = -0.4430, p = 0.0018, n = 47), but not in those treated with placebo or 1500 units.

The passages do not directly settle whether peer review has a role in profiling quality of care; they show that a structured implicit physician review instrument had a single-reviewer intra-class correlation of 0.16–0.26 for COPD and a collection of acute conditions and 0.46 for diabetes and hypertension , and that profiling must reflect true provider performance and requires an appropriate statistical model.

Peer review is described as the gold standard for vetting academic manuscripts, with concerns about lack of expediency, editorial bias, and statistical limitation from small numbers of reviewers, and a computer model compared traditional peer review to post-publication reader review.
No supplied passage directly tests peer review as a method for profiling quality of care.
The passages do not settle whether sports medicine journals are relevant and applicable to practitioners and athletes.

One analysis of original research, short reports, and case reports published in four major sport and exercise medicine journals found that the most common topic was sports science, very few studies related to treatment of injuries and medical conditions, the majority of articles used healthy subjects sampled from the sedentary population, and few studies were carried out on injured participants.

Another compared material on physical activity and management of smoking, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia in medical journals and magazines frequently read by general practitioners.
Another compared OSICS-10 sports medicine diagnoses assigned by a clinical and non-clinical coder.
The passages do not settle whether combining 2-methoxyestradiol can reduce chemotherapeutic dosages in human ovarian cancer treatment.

They show that in two human ovarian cancer cell lines, 2-methoxyestradiol combined with epirubicine or carboplatin produced a significant additive inhibitory effect on proliferation at the lower concentration range of these chemotherapeutics.
The experiments used equimolar 2-methoxyestradiol at 0.8-25 microM with each chemotherapeutic and measured proliferation after four days using the ATP-chemosensitivity test.

The passages do not directly settle whether expert breast pathology assessment is necessary for DCIS management, but they show that secondary pathology assessment changed local recurrence risk assessment in 100 of 350 reviewed DCIS cases (29%) and contributed to a change in treatment recommendation in 93 cases (43%) from 1996 to 2000.
These results are from 481 individuals with DCIS referred to a single regional cancer centre, with pathology review performed on 350 patients (73%), comparing initial and secondary pathology reports.
Current guidelines recommend that a pathologist with expertise in breast disease review all DCIS specimens because of significant variability in pathologic reporting.
Yes, prior benign prostate biopsy was associated with more favorable pathologic features and lower biochemical failure after radical perineal prostatectomy.
The comparison was 203 patients (14.9%) with at least one prior benign prostate biopsy versus 1115 patients with no prior biopsy among 1369 patients with clinically localized prostate cancer.
Prior-biopsy patients had more organ-confined disease (74% vs 64%, P<0.001) and fewer positive margins (9.8% vs 18%), and biochemical failure occurred in 24 (12%) versus 20% of controls (P=0.01).

Overall, the prior-biopsy group had a lower probability of biochemical failure (odds ratio 0.57, P<0.001), and Kaplan-Meier analyses suggested improved biochemical disease-free survival, especially for Gleason sum 7 or greater (P<0.01).
That study covered 17,137 referrals from 10 general practices in the Trent Focus Collaborative Research Network in 2001, of which 90.4% were to the NHS and 9.6% to the private sector.

The comparison was wards in the top fifth versus the bottom fifth for private referral rates, and the NHS referral rate ratio was 1.40 (95% CI 1.15 to 1.71, p=0.001) after adjustment for deprivation and practice.

The supplied passages do not settle whether an 'early adopter of drugs' exists as a general personal trait; among physicians, early adoption of one drug type was not associated with early adoption of another.

In that analysis, general practitioners' adoption of one group of drugs was poorly associated with adoption of others (r ≤ 0.49), and adoption time adjusted for practice size was only weakly associated with other indicators (r = -0.56 to -0.27).

Separately, a survey of 308 customers in two south London gay dance clubs across 3 weekend nights in July 2010 studied club-goers considered to be 'early adopters' of psychostimulant/club drug trends and found mephedrone was added to existing drug repertoires and supplemented established club drugs rather than replacing or displacing them.

The supplied passages do not settle whether adjuvant radiation is necessary for stage III thymoma, showing only that in 45 resected stage III patients radiotherapy did not alter local or distant recurrence rates and 10-year disease-specific survival was 79% with radiation versus 75% without (p = 0.21).
Those results rest on 45 stage III patients who underwent resection, of whom 38 received radiation, with similar baseline prognostic factors between radiated and nonradiated groups.
Yes—socioeconomic status mattered for postpartum women’s unmet learning needs in this study.

Among 1,250 postpartum women recruited in Ontario, Canada, with 890 (71.2%) interviewed 4 weeks after hospital discharge and about 17% of low socioeconomic status, women of low socioeconomic status were significantly more likely than higher-status women to report unmet learning needs related to 9 of 10 topics.
Identified concerns were similar regardless of socioeconomic status, with breastfeeding and signs of infant illness most frequently reported.
For most topics, significantly more women in both groups identified learning needs 4 weeks after discharge than had identified corresponding concerns while in hospital.

The passages do not directly show whether inhaled steroids differ from cromones in hospital admission rates for asthma in children, because the only relevant comparison is between two provinces with different overall medication patterns rather than a head-to-head comparison of children on inhaled steroids versus cromones.

In children aged >=6 years, the province with 93% inhaled steroid use and 5% cromone use had lower average annual total admissions (0.3/1000 vs 1.2/1000, p<0.001), first admissions (0.2/1000 vs 1.0/1000, p<0.001), readmission proportion (6.3% vs 19.3%, p<0.05), and hospital days (0.7/1000 vs 3.8/1000, p<0.001) than the province with 51% inhaled steroid use, 23% cromone use, and 26% cromones plus intermittent steroids.
The differences were in the same direction but less prominent among children 2-5 years of age.
Yes, some U.S. states have higher or lower injury mortality rates than others.

Among 12 states grouped as the six with the highest and six with the lowest road traffic death rates, 74% of the high-road-traffic-death states also had above-average rates of other injuries such as falling, poisoning, drowning, fire, suffocation, homicide, and suicide, while 85% of the low-road-traffic-death states conformed to the converse.
These results used 1983-1995 data covering nine categories of unintentional and four categories of intentional injury.

Yes, a potential role for uterine natural killer cells in irregular endometrial bleeding in menopausal hormone therapy users is supported by significantly increased endometrial CD56+ uNK cells in biopsies obtained during bleeding episodes compared with HT users with no bleeding.
In 117 postmenopausal women taking combined HT, this increase was significant at P<0.001.
The highest level of IL-15 expression was also seen in biopsies taken during bleeding.
No clear relationship between killer Ig like receptor genotype and bleeding on HT was observed.
Yes, grandmultiparity was an independent risk factor for several adverse perinatal outcomes after controlling for potential confounding factors.
The comparison was 25,512 grandmultiparous women versus 265,060 multiparous women aged 30 years or older with singleton deliveries in California from 1997 to 1998.

Grandmultiparous women had significantly higher adjusted odds of abruptio placentae (OR 1.3, 95% CI 1.2-1.5), preterm delivery (OR 1.3, 95% CI 1.2-1.4), fetal macrosomia (OR 1.5, 95% CI 1.4-1.6), neonatal death (OR 1.5, 95% CI 1.3-1.8), postpartum hemorrhage (OR 1.2, 95% CI 1.1-1.3), and blood transfusion (OR 1.5, 95% CI 1.3-1.8).

The supplied passages do not settle whether serum pancreatic lipase should replace serum amylase as a biomarker of acute pancreatitis, although they show improved diagnostic accuracy for serum pancreatic lipase.
In 10,931 patients with 17,531 measurements, initial Emergency Department samples gave an AUC of 0.948 for serum pancreatic lipase versus 0.906 for serum amylase (P<0.05).

At cut-offs of 208 U/L for lipase and 114 U/L for amylase, sensitivity was 90.3% vs 76.8% and specificity was 93% vs 92.6%, and 18.8% of acute pancreatitis patients did not have elevated amylase while only 2.9% did not have elevated serum pancreatic lipase on the first emergency department measurement.
In hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis, serum amylase and lipase supported the diagnosis in 26% and 58% of patients, compared with 58% and 79% in lithiasic acute pancreatitis.
Another passage defined acute pancreatitis as consistent clinical symptoms and elevated amylase and/or lipase levels.

Yes, one study found hamburger consumption was independently associated with increased odds of a history of wheeze and current wheeze, though this is an association rather than a demonstrated causal effect.

In 1321 children (mean age 11.4 years) in Hastings, New Zealand, compared with children who never ate hamburgers, consuming hamburgers less than once a week gave OR 1.44 (95% CI 1.06–1.96) for history of wheeze and OR 1.17 (95% CI 0.80–1.70) for current wheeze, while consuming them 1+ times a week gave OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.07–2.52) for history of wheeze and OR 1.81 (95% CI 1.10–2.98) for current wheeze.
Takeaway consumption 1+ times a week was marginally significantly related to bronchial hyperresponsiveness (OR 2.41, 95% CI 0.99–5.91), and there was no effect on atopy.

Yes—correlated results were possible between two facilities using different quantitative real-time PCR assays for BCRABL, even though RNA isolation, cDNA synthesis, BCR control cell line, and primer/probe sequences differed.
Among 22 BCRABL-positive paired results, the Spearman rank correlation coefficient was r(s)=0.9435 (p<0.00001), and 43 samples were negative at both facilities.
One discordant result occurred for consecutive samples from one patient with low BCRABL copy number due to minimal RNA yield at one laboratory.
No, bedside assessment did not reliably exclude aspiration following acute stroke in this study.
Among 94 consecutive patients admitted within 24 h of stroke onset who underwent videofluoroscopy, 20 (21%) were aspirating, and bedside assessment missed this in 10.

Bedside assessment by a speech and language therapist had a sensitivity of 47%, specificity of 86%, PPV of 50% and NPV of 85% for aspiration, while a weak voluntary cough and any alteration in conscious level gave a sensitivity of 75%, specificity of 72%, PPV of 41% and NPV of 91%.
Yes, in eyes with strabismus amblyopia, Snellen E acuity was higher than Landolt C acuity, with a mean difference of 0.55 lines.
This rests on 39 patients with amblyopia due to strabismus among 100 patients with various eye disorders and 13 healthy volunteers.

The mean decimal values were 0.14 for Landolt C acuity and 0.16 for Snellen E acuity in the strabismus amblyopia eyes, and the mean difference between Landolt C and Snellen E acuity was 0.55 lines with higher values of Snellen E.

Yes, end-tidal carbon dioxide measurement correlates with arterial carbon dioxide in ventilated extremely low birth weight infants in the first week of life, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.81.
Using EtCO2 ranges of 30 to 50 mmHg, capnography identified 84% of instances where PaCO2 was between 35 and 55 mmHg.
No significant relationship was found between AVPR1A microsatellites and hypersexuality in children with a prepubertal and early adolescent bipolar disorder phenotype.

In 83 PEA-BP probands, preferential transmission of AVPR1A GATA or complex repeats to hypersexual or uninhibited people-seeking probands was not significant by the transmission disequilibrium test, and case-control analyses found no significant associations between these phenotypes and the number of repeats.

The family-based analyses had 32 complete biological trios (28 informative families) for the GATA repeat and 34 trios (30 informative families) for the complex repeat, with about 80% power at p<0.05 to detect odds ratios of 5.0 and 4.0 (family-based) and 3.5 and 2.6 (case-control) for allele frequencies of 0.1 and 0.5, respectively.
Yes, interleukin-8 concentration in pancreatic juice discriminated the presence of pancreatic diseases in patients with abdominal pain.

In 118 patients with abdominal pain compatible with pancreatic origin, secretin-stimulated pancreatic juice was collected and analyzed, and multivariate analysis showed interleukin-8 discriminated normal pancreas from chronic pancreatitis (P =.011), pancreatic cancer (P =.044), and presence of pancreatic diseases (P =.007).
Individual cytokine concentrations were not significantly different between chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer.
Hydrophilic guidewires significantly improved technical success rates for SFA stenosis and for iliac and SFA occlusions, but not significantly for iliac stenosis.
The study performed 125 procedures: 25 stenosed and 25 occluded iliac arteries, and 25 stenosed and 50 occluded femoral arteries, using conventional guidewire first and then hydrophilic if needed.

Technical success rates with conventional vs hydrophilic were: iliac stenosis 96% (24/25) vs 100% (no significant difference); iliac occlusion 60% (15/25) vs 96%; femoral stenosis 84% (21/25) vs 100%; femoral occlusion <10 cm 64% (16/25) vs 96%; femoral occlusion >10 cm 48% (12/25) vs 88%.
Significant changes were reported for SFA stenosis and iliac and SFA occlusions.
Yes, in OSA patients who had a successful manual CPAP titration, greater OSA severity predicted requiring high CPAP.
High CPAP (>=12 cm H2O) was required by 2 (6.9%), 6 (5.8%), and 63 (28.6%) patients with mild, moderate, and severe OSA, respectively.
On logistic regression, high CPAP use was 5.90 times more frequent in severe OSA patients after adjustment for the other variables (95% CI 2.67-13.1).

Yes, in this study preoperative tracheobronchoscopy mattered in newborns with esophageal atresia, being clinically useful in 28 of 62 patients (45.2%) and crucial in modifying the surgical approach in 15 of 62 (24.2%).
In 3 of 9 type A patients, TBS revealed an unsuspected proximal fistula (type B), and in 4 patients it found previously undetected respiratory tree malformations.
Carinal fistulas in 14 type C patients were occluded by Fogarty catheter to improve ventilation during repair, and no complications were observed.
The bottom line rests on 62 newborns with esophageal atresia who underwent preoperative TBS from 1997 to 2003, with no comparator group described in the supplied passages.
Yes, there was a difference in deflation rates between 500 Poly Implant Prosthesis prefilled textured saline implants and 500 Mentor Siltex textured saline implants over 4 years.

Cumulative deflation rates for the Poly Implant Prosthesis implants were 1.2% at year 1, 5.6% at year 2, 11.4% at year 3, and 15.4% at year 4, versus 0.2%, 0.6%, 1.6%, and 4.4% for the Mentor implants.

The difference was not statistically significant at year 1 (Fisher's exact test, p>0.05), but it was statistically significant at year 2 (chi-square 13.29; p<0.001), year 3 (chi-square 37.91; p<0.001), and year 4 (chi-square 32.69; p<0.001).
The supplied passages do not settle whether histological features influence the clinical presentation or outcome of pituitary apoplexy.

They show a retrospective analysis of 59 patients with pituitary apoplexy divided into 22 with infarction alone and 37 with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage, in whom presenting symptoms, clinical features, endocrinological status, and outcome were compared between the two groups.
The supplied passages do not settle whether routine chest radiography after transbronchial biopsy is necessary.

In 350 consecutive patients who underwent flexible bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy and routine CXR up to 2 h after the procedure, pneumothorax was diagnosed radiologically in 10 patients (2.9%); 7 had symptoms strongly suggestive of pneumothorax before CXR, including 4 with large (>10%) pneumothorax, and 3 were asymptomatic with only minimal (<=10%) pneumothorax that resolved completely 24 to 48 h later.
No comparison group is reported.
No, fetal gender was not associated with having an emergency department visit for asthma during pregnancy.
Among 109,173 live singleton deliveries, 530 women had visited the ED due to asthma during pregnancy, and fetal gender was not associated with that outcome (OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.85-1.19).
Fetal gender also was not a significant predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had an asthma ED visit during pregnancy.

No, the reported continuity-of-care experience was incomplete: complete in-hospital continuity (preoperative and postoperative assessment) was 57%, follow-up clinic assessment was 3%, and involvement in the decision to operate was 17%.
The population was 159 patients who underwent a vascular procedure at two teaching hospitals in January 2005.

Emergent cases had a higher preoperative assessment rate than others (92% vs 63%, P<.05), and elective previously admitted patients had higher preoperative assessment (78% vs 58%, P<.05) and decision-to-operate involvement (16% vs 4%, P<.05) than same-day admission patients.
Yes, French lay people and psychologists found breaching confidentiality to protect a patient's wife from a sexually transmitted disease more acceptable than physicians did.
In a French study, 144 lay people, 10 psychologists, and 7 physicians rated acceptability across 48 scenarios, with mean ratings of 11.76, 9.28, and 2.90, respectively, on a 0–22 scale.

Lay participants fell into groups finding breaching confidentiality "always acceptable" (n = 14), "depending on the many circumstances" (n = 87), requiring "consultation with an expert" (n = 30), and "never acceptable" (n = 13).
The patient's stated intentions to protect his wife and to inform her of the disease had the greatest impact on acceptability.
Some myomas grow during pregnancy, but many also decrease in size, so myoma growth is not uniform.

Between the third quarter (20-30 weeks) and the last quarter (31 weeks to term), 25% enlarged with a mean increase in volume of 102%±62% while 75% became smaller with a mean decrease of 30%±3%.
Yes, patient-reported HRQOL measures (pain and dysphagia) were independent prognostic factors for survival in advanced NSCLC.
In 391 advanced NSCLC patients, pretreatment HRQOL was measured with the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13 and analyzed with Cox proportional hazards regression.

In the final multivariate model, self-reported pain had HR = 1.11 (95% CI 1.07-1.16; P < 0.001) and dysphagia had HR = 1.12 (95% CI 1.04-1.21; P = 0.003), with a 10-point worse score associated with an 11% and 12% increased likelihood of death, respectively.
Yes, complex coronary lesions were more frequent in patients with diabetes mellitus in the supplied study.

Among 1,014 consecutive patients (281 diabetic, 733 nondiabetic), the prevalence of bifurcation lesions was 9.8% in diabetics versus 4.3% in nondiabetics (P=0.001) and ostial lesions was 38.4% versus 29.2% (P=0.003).
Diabetes mellitus was also an independent predictor of bifurcation lesions (OR=2.27, P=0.004) and ostial lesions (OR=1.40, P=0.027).

The passages do not settle whether pneumologists' skepticism is justified, because the cited result is an association between cytostatic treatment and survival rather than a demonstrated causal effect.

In 190 patients with stage IV or IIIB NSCLC and ECOG performance status 2 or below, 144 received cytostatic treatment and 46 received palliative treatment, and median survival was 31 weeks, with cytostatic treatment associated with survival (HR, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.25-2.76; P=.002).
In patients with ECOG score 2, survival was 15 weeks for cytostatic treatment versus 11 weeks for symptomatic treatment.
