No, first-trimester folic acid use did not protect against congenital heart defects among children with Down syndrome in the cited case-control analysis.

In women with liveborn Down syndrome children in the Slone Epidemiology Center Birth Defects Study (1976-1997), 110 of 223 cases with heart anomalies (49%) and 84 of 184 controls without heart anomalies (46%) used folic acid in the first 12 weeks.
After adjustment, the odds ratio for heart anomalies overall was 0.95 (95% CI 0.61-1.47), with no protective effect separately for conotruncal defects, VSDs, ASDs, or ECDs.
No, frozen section did not alter intraoperative management in patients undergoing thyroidectomy for multinodular thyroid disease.
In 236 patients with multinodular goiter, 135 (57%) had intra-operative frozen section, and in none of these 135 did frozen section alter the intraoperative management.
Of the 135 patients who had frozen section, 4/135 (3%) were subsequently diagnosed with thyroid cancer on permanent histology, and 3 frozen sections were misread as benign, for a sensitivity of 25%.
The passages do not settle whether obstructive sleep apnea affects aerobic fitness.

They show that in a retrospective cohort of 247 patients with OSA compared to normative data from 1.4 million US Air Force tests, individuals with OSA overall had increased VO2max (p<.001), while those with an apnea-hypopnea index greater than 20 had decreased VO2max (p<.001), and no differences in VO2max were observed after medical or surgical therapy.
No, endoaortic balloon occlusion was not shown to be safe for surgical management of the atherosclerotic ascending aorta in this series.

In 52 of 2,172 consecutive patients selected for aortic calcifications or abnormal epiaortic ultrasound, in-hospital death occurred in 25% (13/52) versus 4.2% in all other patients (p<0.0001) and versus an expected risk of 10.5% (p=0.05), and use of endoaortic occlusion was independently associated with in-hospital death (OR 5.609, 95% CI 2.684–11.719).

Stroke on awakening occurred in 3.8% (2/52) versus 0.8% in all other patients (p=0.067), and the balloon had to be replaced by conventional cross-clamping in 19.2% (10/52) because of incomplete occlusion, hindered exposure, or balloon rupture.

No, the long-term results are not equal in all respects: overall scores were similar, but continence score was significantly better in the ABD group, and stool pattern score was better in the TERPT group.
This rests on 41 patients more than 3 years old who underwent a pull-through for Hirschsprung disease (TERPT, n = 20; ABD, n = 21) and were scored with a 15-item long-term outcome questionnaire.
A significant age-at-interview difference was noted, but reanalysis controlling for age showed that age did not significantly affect the long-term scoring outcome between groups.
No—retrieval of lower ureteric stones was achieved without fluoroscopy in most patients in the reported series, although fluoroscopy was required in a minority.
The population was 110 patients with lower ureteral calculi below the upper margin of the sacroiliac joint, with a mean age of 33.5 years and mean stone size of 8.7 mm.

Complete clearance without fluoroscopy was achieved in 99 patients (94.2%), and fluoroscopy was required in 6 patients (4%) for calcified stricture (n=1), duplex system (n=1), narrow and tortuous meatus causing difficulty passing the 5-Fr balloon dilator (n=3), and confirmation of spontaneous passage of the stone (n=1).

Yes, the study identified a KCNQ1 mutation (R14C) that produced no statistically significant differences from wild-type at baseline or after forskolin but showed a marked increase in current and altered kinetics after hypotonic cell swelling/stretch.
In the affected family, atrial fibrillation was present only in older individuals who had developed atrial dilation and who were genotype positive.
Mutation screening was performed in 50 families with AF, and electrophysiological studies compared wild-type and R14C KCNQ1 expressed with KCNE1 in CHO cells.
These results link a genetic defect (KCNQ1 R14C) with an environmental factor (atrial stretch/dilation) in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation.
The supplied passages do not settle whether neck dissection is needed for metastatic carcinoma to cervical nodes from an unknown head and neck primary site.

In 61 patients treated with radiotherapy, there was no statistically significant difference in 8-year overall survival (64.8% for biopsy vs 67.6% for neck dissection, p =.64) or local relapse-free survival (75% vs 74.5%, p =.57) between those who had biopsy (41 patients) and those who had neck dissection (20 patients).

The supplied results do not settle whether supervised colorectal trainees differ from consultants in quality of TME surgery, because the relevant comparison found no statistically significant difference in mesorectal grade (P = 0.717).

In 130 consecutive patients undergoing potentially curative resection for primary rectal adenocarcinoma, 89 operations were performed by consultants and 41 by senior colorectal trainees with consultant supervision.
Good mesorectum was reported in 44 consultant operations (49%) versus 17 trainee operations (41.5%), with no statistically significant difference (P = 0.717).
Local recurrence occurred in 7 consultant operations (7.8%) versus 4 trainee operations (9.5%), also without statistical significance (P = 0.719).

In a retrospective study of 531 patients with ascending aortic aneurysm or ectasia (45–76 mm), 50 underwent size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement using a non-coated Dacron prosthesis; aortic valve replacement was performed in 47, myectomy in 29, and CABG in 13, with 2% hospital mortality.
Postoperative diameters were significantly smaller (CT 55.8±9 to 40.51±6.2 mm; echocardiography 54.1±6.7 to 38.7±7.1 mm; p<0.002) with stable performance at a mean 70-month follow-up.

Reduction ascending aortoplasty with aortic valve surgery has also been evaluated in bicuspid versus tricuspid valve patients , and in a separate report operations included combined aortic valve replacement and reduction aortoplasty in 9 patients, with no ascending aortic reoperations after previous reduction aortoplasties or supracoronary ascending aortic grafts and no late aortic dissections over a median 3.8 years.
The passages do not settle whether the clinical significance of bile duct sludge is different from bile duct stones, but they show some similarities and differences after endoscopic therapy.
In 228 patients undergoing ERCP for suspected choledocholithiasis, bile duct sludge occurred in 14% (31/228) and was more common in females.
After endoscopic clearance, CBD stones recurred in 17% (33/197) of patients with CBD stones versus 16% (5/31) of patients with bile duct sludge (p = 0.99).
CBD dilation was less common in the sludge group, while other known risk factors for recurrent CBD stones were not statistically different between the two groups.

The antismoking advertisement affected non-smokers' perception that smoking in the movie was not OK and smokers' intention to smoke in 12 months, but it did not significantly affect smokers' perception or non-smokers' intention.

Among non-smokers, 47.8% of intervention subjects versus 43.8% of controls thought the smoking in the viewed movie was not OK (p=0.04), while among smokers there was no significant difference (16.5% vs 14.5%, p=0.4).

For intention, a higher percentage of smokers in the intervention group (38.6%) than in the control group (25.6%) said they were likely to be smoking in 12 months (p<0.001), while non-smokers showed no significant difference (1.2% vs 1.6%, p=0.54).
These results come from 3091 cinema patrons aged 12-24 years in three Australian states, of whom 18.6% were current smokers.
Yes, renal warm ischemia over 30 minutes during laparoscopic partial nephrectomy is possible.

In 18 patients who underwent LPN with warm ischemia time >30 min, kidney damage markers and renal function at 1 yr showed complete return to the normal range and no statistical difference between the values at the various time points.

GFR was not significantly different before and 3 mo after surgery, while scintigraphy of the operated kidney was 48.35+/-3.82% before, 36.88+/-8.42% on postoperative day 5, 40.56+/-8.96% at 3 mo, and 42.8+/-7.2% 1 yr after surgery.

Yes, shaving the incision site before spinal surgery increased the postoperative infection rate in a prospective randomized clinical study. In 789 patients scheduled for spinal surgery, 371 were randomly assigned to have the operative site shaved immediately before surgery and 418 were assigned to no presurgical shaving. A postoperative infection developed in 4 patients in the shaved group versus 1 patient in the nonshaved group (P<0.01).

The passages do not directly settle whether breast cancer prognosis is genetically inherited, but they show a familial association: among 2,787 mother-daughter pairs and 831 sister pairs with breast cancer in Sweden, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor prognosis had a 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality than those of a proband with good prognosis (HR, 1.6; 95% CI, 1.2 to 2.2; p for trend 0.002).
The 5-year survival proportion was 87% among daughters whose mothers died within 5 years versus 91% if the mother was alive (p=0.03), and 70% versus 88% among sisters (p=0.001).
The association was slightly stronger among sisters (HR, 1.8; 95% CI, 1.0 to 3.4) than among daughters (HR, 1.6; 95% CI, 1.1 to 2.3).
The introduction notes that a genetic component is established in breast cancer etiology but it is not well known whether genetic traits influence prognostic features.

Yes, the study identified gender differences in some factors associated with delay in seeking help for acute myocardial infarction symptoms among African Americans, although the overall median delay time difference was not significant.
In 61 African American men and women diagnosed with AMI, median delay time was longer for women than men (4.4 hours vs 3.5 hours) but the difference was not significant.

Single women delayed longer than single men (P =.03), and women who were alone when symptoms began delayed longer than women with someone (P =.03), while women who received advice to seek help or call 911 had shorter delays than women not advised (P =.01).

Men at home delayed longer than men who experienced symptoms outside the home (P =.01), men with emergency room insurance delayed longer than men without (P =.03), and men who took an ambulance had shorter delay times than men who took other means of transportation (P =.04).

Yes, a statistically significant but very weak relationship between serum ACE and severe hypoglycaemia frequency was reported in 300 people with Type 1 diabetes not taking renin-angiotensin system blocking drugs.
Spearman's test gave r = 0.115 (P = 0.047), and a negative binomial model gave P = 0.002 but a clinically weak relationship.

The mean incidence of severe hypoglycaemia in the top versus bottom quartiles of ACE activity was 0.5 versus 1.7 episodes per patient-year, but this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.075).
The overall incidence was 0.93 episodes per patient-year.
Yes, reported competence differed for some specific competencies between rural and urban midwives, although the overall proportion reporting competence was broadly similar.

In a comparison of 82 midwives in remote and rural maternity units and 107 midwives in urban hospitals with midwife-led units in Scotland, rural midwives were more likely to report competence for breech delivery (p = 0.001), while more urban midwives reported competence in intravenous fluid replacement (p < 0.001) and initial and discharge examination of the newborn (p < 0.001).
The response rate was 85% for rural midwives and 60% for urban midwives.

Yes, reading comprehension ability can be improved in adults with mild intellectual disabilities, as the intervention programme showed a substantial transfer effect to general text comprehension that was well maintained at follow-up.
The study included 38 adults aged 20–72 years (mean age 36 years) with IQs of 45–69 (mean IQ 58).
There was no significant difference between group and individual instruction conditions, and direct programme effects on strategy tests were substantial except for the questioning strategy.
General reading comprehension ability was best explained by the test of reading comprehension of sentences and only moderately by the strategies trained.

HER2 immunoreactivity provided univariate prognostic information in locally advanced urothelial carcinoma patients receiving adjuvant M-VEC, but it was not an independent prognostic factor in multivariate analysis.

In 114 locally advanced urothelial carcinoma patients receiving surgery alone or adjuvant M-VEC, HER2 immunoreactivity was significantly associated with progression-free survival (p=0.02) and disease-specific overall survival (p=0.005) overall.

Among patients receiving adjuvant M-VEC, HER2 immunoreactivity was a significant prognostic factor for progression-free survival (p=0.03) and disease-specific overall survival (p=0.02) by univariate analysis, but not by multivariate analysis, and not for patients receiving watchful waiting.
No, in this study family history of hyperlipidemia was not related to serum lipid levels in school children, so it does not appear reliable for choosing whom to screen.
The study included 2096 school children in Ankara (1043 male, 1053 female; mean age 9.03 years) whose demographic properties and serum lipid levels were obtained.
Serum cholesterol was >=200 mg/dL in 135 subjects and serum LDL-cholesterol was >=130 mg/dL in 83 subjects, while 64.4% reported a family history of hyperlipidemia.
No relations were found between family history and serum lipid levels.

The passages do not directly show that the postoperative pain level can be predicted preoperatively; they show that significant postoperative pain was correlated with prior history of surgical pain, duration of prior pain, intensity of preoperative pain, and depression.

Yes, body diffusion-weighted MR imaging is helpful for detecting uterine endometrial cancer when used in addition to conventional nonenhanced MR imaging.

In 23 patients, T2-weighted images alone detected endometrial cancer in 19 patients (83% sensitivity), and adding DW and fused DW/T2-weighted images identified cancers in 3 of the remaining 4 patients, giving an overall detection sensitivity of 96%.
The mean ADC value of endometrial cancer was significantly lower than those of normal endometrium, myometrium, leiomyoma, and adenomyosis (p<0.05).

In 218 preschool children stratified into a specialised phonologic awareness training program to prevent dyslexia or a general perception training program, with 131 compared in first grade, the whole group showed only a slight difference between the two modalities in writing abilities.

Yes, routine laboratory markers—specifically MCV and the AST/ALT ratio—are useful for differentiating nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) from alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH).
In 95 patients with steatohepatitis (58 NASH, 37 ASH) diagnosed by liver biopsy and alcohol history (<140 g/week), MCV was elevated in 53% of ASH patients and normal in all NASH patients (P<0.0001).

The passages do not settle whether pectins are causally involved, but they show that cold acclimation is associated with increases in leaf pectin content and low-methylated pectin content, and de-acclimation reverses most of these effects.

The passages do not settle whether c-kit expression has a diagnostic role in HBV-induced chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, or HCC.

The supplied passages do not settle whether chest wall irradiation should be included after mastectomy for node-negative breast cancer.

A separate retrospective analysis included 92 internal or central-breast node-negative tumours treated with mastectomy and external irradiation of the internal mammary chain at 50 Gy but reported no outcome data.
The passages do not settle whether confined placental mosaicism (CPM) accounts for adverse perinatal outcomes in IVF pregnancies.

Fetal chromosomal anomalies were 4.3% versus 2.4% (odds ratio 1.81, 95% CI 0.95-3.42), also not statistically significant.
The passages do not directly show that laparoscopic surgery decreases the risk of atrial fibrillation after foregut surgery; they show an association with lower risk.

Among adults, 38% had a healthy BMI, 38% were overweight, and 22% were obese, but 28% of those with a BMI of 25 or greater considered their weight 'just about right'.

The beta1Ser49Gly polymorphism differed significantly, beta1Gly49 homozygotes had a higher TTN risk than beta1Ser49 allele carriers (OR 18.5; 95% CI 1.5-229; p = 0.023), and the ADRB2 TACC haplotype (T-47C, A46G, C79G, C491T) was also significantly associated with TTN (p = 0.048).
Yes, physicians' specialty significantly influenced both the frequency and depth of medication history documentation in patients' medical records.

In a cross-sectional assessment at a 900-bed teaching hospital in Ibadan, Nigeria, 123 physicians documented medication histories for 900 randomly selected patients stratified across nine specialties (Cardiology, Chest, Dermatology, Endocrine, Gastroenterology, Haematology, Neurology, Psychiatry and Renal).

The comparison involved 67 patients allocated to a urologist with 25 prior TURPs (24 patients), a urologist with 50 prior TURPs (24 patients), or a senior urologist with vast TURP experience (19 patients).
No, wandering and physically nonaggressive agitation (PNA) are not equivalent.

In 181 ambulatory residents with dementia, factor analysis yielded a one-factor solution for wandering (explained variance 43.66%) and a two-factor solution for PNA (explained variance 53.45%), and wandering correlated with PNA Factor 1 at r=0.68 (p<0.001) and Factor 2 at r=0.26 (p<0.01).

The supplied results do not settle whether bezafibrate prevents colon cancer in patients with coronary artery disease, because colon cancer occurred in 8 of 1506 bezafibrate patients (0.53%) versus 17 of 1505 placebo patients (1.13%), with a two-sided Fisher p=0.07 and a multivariable hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.2-1.1).

The comparison rests on 3011 patients without any cancer diagnosis in the randomized, double-blind Bezafibrate Infarction Prevention Study, who received 400 mg bezafibrate retard or placebo once daily.

Yes, older patients who refused participation in a Dutch self-management intervention differed from those who agreed: refusers were more restricted in mobility, lived further from the intervention location, and more often had a partner.
Among 361 invited older patients from a Dutch outpatient clinic, 267 (74%) refused participation.
No differences were found between refusers and participants in level of education, age, or gender.
The main reasons refusers gave were lack of time, travel distance, and transport problems.
The passages do not settle whether endothelin-1 has a causal role in hemodynamic changes during hemodialysis, but they show that intradialytic ET-1 levels change in parallel with hemodynamic status.

Pre-dialysis ET-1 levels were significantly higher in dialysis patients than in 15 healthy controls (P<0.001) but were comparable among the three HD groups.
No, risk factors for suicidal behavior did not differ by affective disorder polarity in the NIMH Collaborative Depression Study.

In 909 participants meeting criteria for major depressive and bipolar disorders followed through 4204 mood cycles, age, hopelessness, and active substance abuse, but not polarity, predicted suicidal behavior.
During follow-up, 40 cycles ended in suicide and 384 cycles contained at least one suicide attempt, and the effects of risk factors did not differ by polarity.

The passages do not settle whether breast is best for children with a family history of atopy, but they show that breast-feeding was related to lower levels of childhood illness in such children.

The absolute difference in death rates between lowest and highest employment grades increased from 12.9 per 1000 person years at ages 40-64 to 38.3 per 1000 at ages 70-89.
A non-work based measure (car ownership) had an independent association with mortality equal in magnitude to employment grade after retirement.

The passages do not settle whether cardiopulmonary bypass temperature affects postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome; they show that both cold (26±5°C) and warm (35±1°C) CPB groups had reduced TT4 and TT3 for up to 5 days after CPB, reduced free T3 for up to 3 days, elevated reverse T3 on postoperative days 1 and 3, and unchanged TSH.

The passage does not settle whether marginally acceptable hearts are suitable for transplantation.

Actuarial survival was 86.2% versus 64.6% at 1 and 2 years for FAC>50% versus FAC<50% donors, respectively (p = NS).

2.89 arterial blood gases per infant per call night (0.33 more, p =.02; $169 more per call night), while there was no difference between interns and residents in ordering radiographs or electrolytes.

In 51 air-dried, Diff-Quik-stained fine-needle aspirates of palpable breast lesions with biopsy-proven diagnoses of NPBD (34 cases) or PBD (17 cases), the only cytologic feature significantly different between PBD and NPBD was a swirling pattern of epithelial cells, seen in 13 of 17 PBD cases (76%) and 12 of 34 NPBD cases (35%) (P = 0.008).

The passages do not settle whether magnetic resonance can substitute for diagnostic arthroscopy in occult post-traumatic knee lesions.

In 70 patients with a history of acute musculoskeletal trauma, negative conventional radiographs, pain and limited joint movements, MRI identified 25 bone bruises, 33 subchondral injuries and 35 osteochondral injuries, while arthroscopy depicted 45 osteochondral and 19 chondral injuries.

A separate prospective study aimed to analyze the practicability of replacing arthroscopy by MRI in diagnosis of cartilage lesions, noting that MRI sensitivity ranges from 15% to 96% and that cartilage lesions diagnosed by MRI were not confirmed in arthroscopy.

Pilocytic astrocytomas (four cases) showed lacy clusters of small-to-medium sized vessels with intact vessel wall integrity.

In 149,177 elderly Medicare beneficiaries with acute myocardial infarction in 1994 or 1995, admission to a top-ranked hospital was associated with lower adjusted 30-day mortality (odds ratio, 0.87; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.76 to 1.00; P=0.05).
